name: MAX941CSA+
title: MAX941/MAX942/MAX944: single, dual and quad high-speed, low-power 3 V/5 V rail-to-rail-input comparators
summary: A family of single-supply comparators for 3 V and 5 V systems, running from 2.7 V to 6 V: the MAX941 holds one comparator, the MAX942 two and the MAX944 four. Propagation delay is 80 ns typical at 5 mV overdrive with about 350 µA per comparator; the input common-mode range reaches past both rails, internal hysteresis gives clean switching, and the outputs drive CMOS or TTL without pull-ups. The MAX941 adds an output latch and a shutdown pin. MAX941CSA is the single in 8-pin SO, rated 0 °C to +70 °C.

circuits.title: 3.3V digitally controlled threshold detector
circuits.description: An 8-bit serial DAC sets the comparison level. Its output C drives IN+ of a MAX941 and the signal to test goes to IN-, so OUT is high while the signal is below the DAC level and low above it. DAC and comparator share one 3.3 V rail; the DAC's reference input is tied to that rail.
notes: SHDN and LATCH sit on V+: SHDN high runs the part and LATCH high keeps the latch transparent.

circuits.title: Line transceiver application
circuits.description: Receiving end of a coax line on a 3 V supply. Two equal 20 kΩ resistors split V+ to put IN- at mid-supply; the line drives IN+ through 10 kΩ. OUT swings between 0 V and 3 V as the line crosses the mid-supply level, and the built-in hysteresis keeps the edges clean.
notes: SHDN and LATCH sit on V+: SHDN high runs the part and LATCH high keeps the latch transparent.

operation.text: Each comparator has fixed internal hysteresis, so there are two trip points: one for a rising and one for a falling differential input, and the output does not chatter when the inputs sit close together or move slowly. No external hysteresis resistors are needed. With IN- held at 0 V and IN+ swept, the output rises at VTRIP+ and falls at VTRIP-; swapping the inputs gives the same picture with the output inverted.

The MAX941 has an internal latch, controlled by the high-impedance LATCH pin. With LATCH high the latch is transparent and the comparator behaves as if it were absent; pulling LATCH low stores the current output state. The setup, hold, pulse-width and latch-delay timings must all be met when the latch is used.

Timing is referred to LATCH crossing V+/2 and OUT crossing V+/2. The differential input must be settled tS before LATCH falls and stay put for tH after. tPD runs from the input change to OUT crossing; tLPW is the width of a high pulse on LATCH; tLPD runs from LATCH rising to OUT crossing.

SHDN low shuts the MAX941 down: supply current drops under 30 µA and OUT floats (high impedance). SHDN is a high-impedance input; tie it to V+ for normal running. LATCH must be high when coming out of shutdown, or the output state is undefined.

Each input passes through a 2.5 kΩ resistor, and between the two resistors sit four back-to-back diodes, which hold the differential voltage reaching the internal circuit to at most 4VF (VF about 0.7 V at +25 °C). Past 4VF of differential input, extra current flows out of IN+ and into IN-; below it the input current equals IB. The same protection lets the common-mode range go past both rails, and the output is correct as long as at least one input is inside the common-mode range.

The output is current driven: during a transition a large ISOURCE or ISINK is switched to the pin for a fast slew, and at the final VOH or VOL level the current drops to a small holding level, saving power. Slew rate depends linearly on load capacitance, so a heavy capacitive load slows the output edge, which can help where fast edges would cause interference. The outputs pull within 0.4 V of either rail with no pull-up or pull-down, suiting CMOS and TTL logic, and every input and output pin withstands a continuous short to either rail.

The high gain-bandwidth calls for care to reach full speed: a solid, low-inductance ground plane; a decoupling capacitor, for example 0.1 µF ceramic, right at V+ with short leads and adequate bandwidth; short input and output leads to avoid parasitic feedback; and the part soldered to the board rather than socketed.
